messages:
incident-bot: Pager duty - SEV2: sustained high request latencies on /v1/generate (prod), queue_depth=1123, p95 latency 4.8s, affected pool: gpu-pool-a. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/queue-overload
sara: Acknowledging, I'm oncall. What customers impacted? any 5xx spike?
jamal: Not seeing elevated 5xx, just timeouts at gateway and request queueing. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/gpu-pool-a - pods in pool are at 100% GPU util but several pods stuck Pending for node provisioning. Current HPA target: gpu_utilization 70%.
nate: Quick check: `kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide | grep gpu-pool-a | awk '{print $1,$3,$4,$5}'` shows ~6 Running, 9 Pending -> reasons: ImagePullBackOff + InitContainer timeout on warmup script.
maya: Confirming logs from k8s: `Events: Warning FailedScheduling  (0s)  default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient GPUs, 7 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.` So scheduler waiting for capacity; autoscaler not yet added nodes because cloud provider quota hit for that region.
ml-sre: Hypothesis 1: cloud quota/slow node provisioning causing HPA to not meet target -> queue piles up. Hypothesis 2: warmup script for model container blocking readiness probe leading to Pending and slower lifecycle.
jamal: Live mitigation: 1) apply ingress rate-limiting to protect control plane: `kubectl apply -f rate-limit-protect.yaml -n prod` 2) reroute a small % (10%) of traffic to fallback model (cpu-backed) to buy time 3) request immediate capacity bump with cloud-ops. I'm running commands now.
sara: Jamal — confirm small rollback to fallback model route and add quota request ticket to cloud-ops with priority P0.
jamal: Done reroute: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood/route -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","weights":{"gpu":0.9,"cpu-fallback":0.1}}'` and filed cloud ticket CHG-9871 with screenshot of https://grafana/alerts.
nate: For warmup: we can kill stuck init pods to let new pods land on already-provisioned nodes: `kubectl delete pod <stuck-init> -n prod`. Doing that on two pods now.
maya: Node provisioning now progressing after quota bump from cloud-ops (they added 4 gpus). New nodes appearing, pods transitioning to Running. Queue depth dropping from 1123 -> 410 in last 5m.
ml-sre: Note: KV cache miss rate spiked during the event (~82%). When new model instances come up they incur heavy cold-start work and cache repopulation adds load. Consider background pre-warm job for next-gen rollout.
product-oncall: Heads up: one customer (acme-inc) reported visible slowdown in chat product. CS notified and offered status update.
cs-rep: Logged customer impact and ETA to acme-inc: 30m for full recovery, they asked to be informed if slowdown persists.
sara: Summary: immediate mitigations applied (ingress rate-limit, 10% fallback traffic, killed stuck init pods, cloud quota bumped). Metrics improving but still monitoring. Handoff: I'll stay for next 20m then hand off to nate. Please keep logs and timeline in the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2791234567. Next steps: follow-up RCA to cover autoscaler quotas, init script timeout, pre-warm strategy. :thumbsup:
